What was wrong / what it is: All FiveCrux revenue ran through Tebex. @paypal/checkout-server-sdk sat in package.json unused and is deprecated by PayPal.
Fix / What was built: Added lib/paypal.ts: supported @paypal/paypal-server-sdk client, EUR currency, and hand-rolled webhook signature verification (the SDK ships none). Certificate host is pinned to paypal.com.
Why: Client has an approved PayPal business account; Tebex is being removed entirely.
Verified: tsc + build clean; check-paypal.mjs probe green

What was wrong / what it is: No payment rail existed outside Tebex for the cart (ad slots, featured slots, subscriptions, props).
Fix / What was built: POST /api/paypal/order prices the cart SERVER-side and returns only an order id; /api/paypal/capture captures then provisions; /api/paypal/webhook handles capture, refund, denied and reversed events.
Why: The buyer must never be able to send an amount - price and coupon are re-validated on the server.
Verified: End-to-end tested locally on PGlite with a seeded cart

What was wrong / what it is: The 687-line Tebex webhook held all the logic that grants what people pay for and reverses it on refund. Duplicating it for PayPal would let the two drift apart.
Fix / What was built: Extracted verbatim into lib/provisioning.ts (Tebex webhook 688 -> 538 lines). PayPal calls the same functions.
Why: What a buyer receives must not depend on which payment provider was used.
Verified: tsc clean; both webhooks exercised locally

What was wrong / what it is: Checkout redirected to a Tebex hosted basket.
Fix / What was built: Cart renders PayPal buttons. createOrder asks our server, which prices the cart and re-validates the coupon or creator code, and returns only an order id.
Why: Removes Tebex from the platform's own checkout.
Verified: Verified in browser: 2-item cart totals EUR 335, PayPal + card buttons render

What was wrong / what it is: Side-banner purchase went through Tebex baskets.
Fix / What was built: Rewritten onto PayPal Orders v2. The DB reservation lock (stops two buyers taking the same position) and release-on-failure are unchanged. Duration validation now comes from the price table.
Why: A failed payment must not hold a scarce slot hostage.
Verified: Reservation and release paths tested locally

Item: Tebex removed from every payment path
What was wrong / what it is: Tebex was both the payment rail AND the price database for platform placements.
Fix / What was built: Nothing new is paid for through Tebex. Seller assets still redirect to the seller's own store, so seller money never passes through FiveCrux.
Why: Client instruction: remove Tebex completely.
Files changed: 14 files across cart, side banners and script detail
Verified: grep confirms no Tebex call on any platform payment path

Item: Refund webhook looked up the wrong record
What was wrong / what it is: On a refund event resource.id is the REFUND id, never the capture id - so the lookup could fail to find its order and silently skip revoking the entitlement AND blocking the account.
Fix / What was built: Read the capture from the rel="up" link first, then supplementary_data.related_ids.capture_id. resource.id is used only for DENIED and REVERSED, which really are capture-shaped events.
Why: This defeated the entire chargeback-blocking feature on the exact event that triggers it.
Verified: Found by reading PayPal's payload docs; checked against their refund example

What was wrong / what it is: Nothing stopped a sandbox PayPal key being deployed live - payments would silently not be real.
Fix / What was built: assertNotSandboxInProduction() throws at request time unless PAYPAL_ENVIRONMENT=live. Deliberately not at module scope, which broke next build (Next imports every route with NODE_ENV=production).
Why: A store taking fake payments looks identical to one taking real ones until reconciliation.
Verified: Build verified clean after moving the guard off module scope

What was wrong / what it is: Buyers were paying, filing a chargeback (money back, goods kept), then coming straight back to repeat it. Revoking the entitlement was all that happened - nothing stopped the next attempt.
Fix / What was built: A chargeback webhook now blocks the account. A block is READ-ONLY, not a ban: they can still sign in and browse, but cannot buy, submit or enter anything.
Why: Reported by the client as an ongoing, repeating loss.
Files changed: lib/provisioning.ts, lib/api-auth.ts, middleware.ts, auth.ts, lib/db/schema.ts, drizzle/0020
Verified: Verified: blocked account can browse; every mutating route returns 403

What was wrong / what it is: The codebase has no single write chokepoint - only 9 API routes use requireUser while 61 call getServerSession directly, and 62 routes have mutating handlers.
Fix / What was built: The middleware matcher was widened from /api/admin/* to /api/* and refuses every mutating request from a blocked user (auth routes exempt), plus assertNotBlocked() fresh DB reads on the money paths.
Why: A single-point check would have missed 53 routes.
Verified: Route-by-route probe: no mutating route reachable while blocked

Item: Blacklist tab in the admin panel
What was wrong / what it is: The blocking API existed but nothing surfaced it - staff had to call the endpoint by hand.
Fix / What was built: Admin > Blacklist shows who is blocked, why, when, and whether the block was automatic (chargeback, badged red) or manual, with one-click unblock and a manual block form.
Why: Client asked for chargebackers to be visible in the admin panel.
Verified: Verified in browser as admin

What was wrong / what it is: Ad slot, featured slot and side banner prices were read live from the Tebex store - Tebex was the price database, not just the payment rail.
Fix / What was built: All 27 prices were read from the live store before the switch and captured exactly in lib/platform-pricing.ts (ads 40-1350, featured 20-400, banners 49.99-149.99).
Why: Nothing changed for a buyer during the migration.
Verified: Compared against live /api/advertise/pricing output before cut-over

What was wrong / what it is: Once hardcoded, changing any price needed a code deploy.
Fix / What was built: Admin > Pricing: DB-backed prices with pill switching between Ad slots / Featured slots / Side banners, unsaved-change dots, per-row reset-to-default and a sticky save bar. Applies to the next checkout, no deploy.
Why: Client asked for all prices to be admin-managed, with PayPal used only as the payment rail.
Verified: Verified: price changed in admin, new value quoted on the public page

Item: Price fallback fails expensive, not cheap
What was wrong / what it is: If the price table could not be read, a naive fallback would have priced paid placements at zero.
Fix / What was built: loadPrices() never throws: on any DB error the built-in defaults stand.
Why: A database outage must never make a paid placement free.
Verified: Tested with the table unavailable locally - defaults served, nothing free

Item: Admin price change did not reach the website
What was wrong / what it is: Reported: a price changed in admin showed there, but the site kept quoting the old one. Three cache layers, all left over from the slow Tebex call: revalidate=60, a hardcoded Cache-Control: s-maxage=60 stale-while-revalidate=300, and plain client fetches.
Fix / What was built: All three removed. The response header was the dangerous one - removing only revalidate looked fixed locally because dev has no CDN in front of it.
Why: On Vercel the edge would still have served the old price to real buyers.
Verified: Verified by asserting on the response headers, not just the rendered page

What was wrong / what it is: Nothing stopped a slipped decimal turning EUR 40 into EUR 4000, a negative price, or a junk package key.
Fix / What was built: PATCH rejects unknown keys, non-finite or negative amounts, and anything over 100,000. Founder/admin only.
Why: This is money, and a moderator has no business setting what things cost.
Verified: Probed with bad payloads: all rejected with 400

What was wrong / what it is: Nothing on FiveCrux renews itself - an ad slot, featured slot or side banner simply stops. The first sign was the placement quietly vanishing, which reads as a bug, and by then the seller has lost days they paid for.
Fix / What was built: The profile now shows what is running out, how long is left (hours under a day, days above), and a Renew button that goes straight to buying the same thing again. Covers all three paid products.
Why: Client asked for an in-portal expiry notice with a buy-again path.
Verified: Verified in browser with seeded near-expiry placements

What was wrong / what it is: Auto-charging would need PayPal billing plans, which cannot carry coupons or a multi-item cart - both of which work today.
Fix / What was built: Chose expiry warnings plus one-click re-buy instead, and recorded the trade-off.
Why: Discussed with the client; warnings preserve existing discount and cart behaviour.
Verified: n/a

Item: All paid advertiser flows switched off
What was wrong / what it is: The payment gateway rejected the advertising business. Without a gateway the platform could not process payments at all, which would also have killed asset sales.
Fix / What was built: Advertising disabled across 18 audited surfaces - paid API routes refuse with 410; side rails, Advertise CTA, home hero promo and ad cards hidden. Everything COMMENTED OUT, not deleted, tagged ADS-DISABLED 2026-08-16 so restore is a straight uncomment.
Why: Client instruction: comment out, never delete.
Verified: Automated check-ads-disabled.mjs probe over every disabled surface

What was wrong / what it is: notFound() inside a still-registered route streams a 200 with the 404 UI painted inside it - so the page was technically still live.
Fix / What was built: Renamed the route to a private folder (_advertise.disabled) so Next.js never registers it and the router 404s before rendering.
Why: A 200 on a disabled page is indexable and reads as available.
Verified: curl confirms a real 404 status code

Item: The app had no 404 page at all
What was wrong / what it is: app/not-found.tsx did not exist, so notFound() had nothing to render anywhere on the site.
Fix / What was built: Created it. Black-on-orange text (7.06:1 contrast) rather than white (2.80:1, below AA).
Why: Found while disabling routes; deliberately kept even after the ads restore.
Verified: Contrast measured, not eyeballed

What was wrong / what it is: Client asked for both back once the PayPal account was approved - the compliance blocker was gone.
Fix / What was built: Done as git reverts of the two disabling commits rather than hand-uncommenting ~30 files, so the restored code is byte-identical to the original rather than an approximation. not-found.tsx and two unrelated fixes were deliberately kept.
Why: Hand-uncommenting 30 files invites silent drift.
Verified: tsc and build clean; site re-verified after restore

Item: Side rails were the page's only side margin
What was wrong / what it is: Reducing SideAdsFrame to just {children} when ads were disabled welded content to both screen edges and clipped the rightmost cards off-screen on wide viewports.
Fix / What was built: The frame is now a real centered container with padding and a max width, so all 10 pages that mount it are fixed without touching any call site.
Why: A layout regression only visible on the live page, not in any test.
Verified: Checked at 1440px and wider

Item: Empty hero after ads were disabled
What was wrong / what it is: The hero is fed ONLY by paid featured slots, so disabling ads left the homepage opening straight onto a card grid with no hero.
Fix / What was built: A first attempt filled it with ordinary listings - reverted on client instruction, because that gives away the exact thing being sold. A brand banner was used instead, which holds nothing sellable.
Why: Client: the hero is the advertising product; filling it free undercuts it when it returns.
Verified: Visually verified

What was wrong / what it is: The paid Featured Spotlight and the brand/search banner both rendered, one above the other.
Fix / What was built: Kept the paid hero, commented out the banner with the trade-off noted next to it: if no featured slots are sold the page opens on the chip row with no hero, one uncomment away from being covered again.
Why: Client asked to keep only the first hero.
Verified: Verified in browser

What was wrong / what it is: The Featured row and the hero spotlight both fell back to the entire catalogue when no paid featured slots were active, so ordinary assets appeared labelled FEATURED. Expired slots also lingered because expiry relied on a lazy client-triggered job.
Fix / What was built: Both bound strictly to real featured items, plus a live end-date guard (featuredEndDate IS NULL OR > now()). The same leak was found and fixed on the giveaways hero and on ads.
Why: Mislabelling ordinary listings as paid placements devalues the paid product.
Verified: Verified with and without active featured slots

Item: Switched from Inter to Chakra Petch
What was wrong / what it is: Inter is the most-used UI font on the web and the default an AI reaches for - it read as generic SaaS and said nothing about FiveM.
Fix / What was built: Chakra Petch site-wide. It ships no weight above 700, and the codebase uses font-extrabold/font-black in ~78 places across 23 files, which the browser would synthesise and render muddy at display sizes. Both utilities are capped to the real 700 in one CSS rule instead of 78 edits.
Why: Client picked it from four rendered options.
Verified: Rendered comparison of all four candidates before the choice

Item: Cover images stopped loading on the live site
What was wrong / what it is: Vercel's image optimizer returned 402 OPTIMIZED_IMAGE_REQUEST_PAYMENT_REQUIRED - the plan's source-image quota was spent. Covers that still appeared were coming from browser cache, which is why the failures looked random.
Fix / What was built: Self-hosted optimizer at /api/img with a custom next/image loader (sharp). images.unoptimized was rejected: the live catalogue is 154 covers, 193 MB, 1.28 MB average, so a 12-card grid would have shipped 8.2 MB of originals.
Why: Tebex's CDN ignores resize parameters (?w=, ?width=, ?format= all return the same 5.3 MB file), so there was nothing upstream to lean on.
Verified: Measured: 8.2 MB -> 140 KB per grid

What was wrong / what it is: The 8-second loading guard depended on [isFetching] and cleared its timer on cleanup, so any query that flapped - a retrying 403, for instance - reset the timer before it could fire. The guarantee never held.
Fix / What was built: Made the timeout absolute, started once on mount.
Why: A moderator could not use the admin panel at all.
Verified: Measured: never loaded -> 4.4s

Item: Moderators were locked out of their own queues
What was wrong / what it is: /api/admin/scripts and /api/admin/giveaways hand-rolled admin||founder, shutting moderators out of the exact content queues the role exists for.
Fix / What was built: Both now accept moderator, with the error text corrected to "Forbidden: Staff access required".
Why: A moderation role that cannot moderate is not a role.
Verified: 14/14 API assertions: moderator allowed on content, still refused on users/pricing/site-content

What was wrong / what it is: Even with the APIs fixed, the client hooks for scripts and giveaways still gated on admin||founder, so a moderator's Pending / Assets / Giveaways tabs showed nothing.
Fix / What was built: Client hooks aligned with the API role lists.
Why: The API fix on its own was invisible to the user.
Verified: Verified in browser: all three tabs now carry content

Item: Ads tab 403'd in a retry loop
What was wrong / what it is: useAdminAds allowed moderators, but its endpoint is /api/admin/advertisements, which is admin/founder only. (/api/admin/ads exists and does allow moderator, but nothing calls it.)
Fix / What was built: Ads is a paid placement, so the tab now follows Users / Pricing / Home Content and is admin-only.
Why: The retry loop was the remaining cause of the slow moderator load.
Verified: Zero 4xx on /api/admin/* for both roles after the fix

Item: A dead props query held the dashboard open
What was wrong / what it is: useAdminProps queried /api/admin/props, which returns 410 while the props feature is off. Retrying a dead endpoint kept the loading gate open.
Fix / What was built: Query disabled, with a marker comment so it flips back on restore.
Why: Admin load was 16.3s, almost all of it this.
Verified: Measured: 16.3s -> 2.6s

Item: Pricing tab shown to moderators who cannot open it
What was wrong / what it is: gated: true does not mean what it looks like - its filter is !gated || isModerator || isFounder, so a gated item still shows to moderators. It cannot express "founder/admin only" at all.
Fix / What was built: Added an explicit adminOnly flag honoured in the filter. The gate is admin OR founder, matching requireRole(["admin","founder"]) on the endpoint - isFounder alone would have hidden the screen from a plain admin who is allowed to use it.
Why: Clicking the tab did nothing.
Verified: Verified per role: moderator 7 tabs, admin 11

What was wrong / what it is: console.log("Admin Dashboard - Ads:") ran on every render, and /api/admin/advertisements logged every caller's roles.
Fix / What was built: Removed.
Why: Noise in the production console, and roles are needless detail in server logs.
Verified: tsc clean

What was wrong / what it is: JSON-LD on asset, prop and giveaway detail pages injected user-supplied title and description via JSON.stringify, which does not escape "<" - a "</script>" in a title was a breakout.
Fix / What was built: Added lib/json-ld.ts safeJsonLd() and routed all three pages through it.
Why: Found in a happy-path plus unhappy-path UAT sweep.
Verified: Payload probe: breakout no longer possible

What was wrong / what it is: /api/scripts, /api/scripts/[id], /api/giveaways and /api/giveaways/[id] returned seller emails, creator emails and embedded winner emails to anyone.
Fix / What was built: Stripped from public responses; owner and staff still see them on detail.
Why: PII exposure on unauthenticated read endpoints.
Verified: Responses re-checked as anonymous, owner and staff

Item: Listing validation checked presence, not value
What was wrong / what it is: Asset submit and edit validated that fields EXISTED, so a negative price went live, a non-numeric price 500'd, and an empty title or unknown category slug (orphan listing) were all accepted.
Fix / What was built: Shared lib/validate-listing.ts used by both POST /api/scripts and PATCH.
Why: Same class as the props NaN price and the creator-code missing cap, all fixed together.
Verified: Bad-input probes all rejected

Item: Creator codes charged full price silently
What was wrong / what it is: Checkout applied creator codes with applyCoupon (the wrong endpoint), best-effort - so an unapplied code charged the buyer full price while the order and creator commission were booked against a discount that never happened.
Fix / What was built: Switched to the creator-code endpoint, reject checkout if it is rejected, and recompute payable and discount from the real basket total.
Why: The recorded order must match what the buyer was actually charged.
Verified: Order and redemption totals reconciled

Item: Creator-code edit had no percentage cap
What was wrong / what it is: The CREATE route capped the discount percentage; the EDIT route did not, so a 150% discount could be saved and take an order total to zero.
Fix / What was built: Cap added to edit.
Why: Found sweeping for the same drift class as the side-banner duration bug.
Verified: 150% payload now rejected

Item: Approved giveaways could not be entered
What was wrong / what it is: approveGiveaway left status at 'pending', so the entry endpoint 400'd every entry - nobody could enter an approved giveaway.
Fix / What was built: Sets status 'active'.
Why: Found in a full backend audit.
Verified: Entry flow tested end to end

Item: Editing a live asset took it offline
What was wrong / what it is: After auto-approve was introduced, editing a LIVE asset re-queued it to pending - an unmonitored queue - so the asset disappeared from the site.
Fix / What was built: Edits now update in place; only rejected assets need re-approval.
Why: Silent removal of a seller's live listing.
Verified: Edit-while-live verified

What was wrong / what it is: The integer PK generator used floor(Date.now()/1000) + rand(0..9999), which collided for two adds in the same second.
Fix / What was built: Full 32-bit random. The same fix was applied to the checkout id generator.
Why: An intermittent 500 that looked random to the user.
Verified: Repeated same-second adds no longer collide

What was wrong / what it is: The cap was read as snake_case while the value was camelCase maxEntries, so it was always undefined.
Fix / What was built: Read the correct key.
Why: A cap that silently does nothing is worse than no cap.
Verified: Cap enforced in test

What was wrong / what it is: Checkout validated durationWeeks against a hardcoded [1,2,3] while the live packages were 1/2/4 weeks - buying the 4-week banner failed with "Invalid duration".
Fix / What was built: Dropped the stale list; the real validation is resolving the duration to a real package. Adding a duration now needs no code change.
Why: First instance of the hardcoded-vs-live drift class that was then swept app-wide.
Verified: 4-week purchase completes

Item: Ad category validated against a stale list
What was wrong / what it is: Both the client form and the admin route validated ad category against hardcoded [scripts, giveaways, props], rejecting real categories (Maps, Vehicles and so on) that the dropdown itself offered.
Fix / What was built: Validated against the live category list.
Why: Same drift class as above.
Verified: Every dropdown value now accepted

Item: Edits and new items did not appear
What was wrong / what it is: Home, marketplace, category, script-detail, giveaway-detail, props and giveaways clients all reused the ISR SSR seed and skipped the client refetch, so the list showed old data while the API already returned the new data.
Fix / What was built: All refetch live after mount; detail pages refresh in the background with no spinner and keep the seed on failure.
Why: Reported repeatedly as "my change isn't showing".
Verified: Verified by editing an item and reloading

Item: The CDN served stale catalogue data
What was wrong / what it is: /api/scripts, /api/giveaways, /api/props, /api/featured-scripts, /api/categories and /api/frameworks carried s-maxage=60 on mutable data. Client-side no-store did not bypass the shared CDN copy.
Fix / What was built: Dropped the CDN cache on mutable endpoints; props, categories and frameworks made force-dynamic.
Why: This was the real fix - the client-side change alone only looked like one.
Verified: Response headers asserted

What was wrong / what it is: /scripts filters entirely client-side but only had the SSR seed (newest ~24) to filter, so a category whose items were not in that seed showed "0 assets" even though the API returned them.
Fix / What was built: Always fetch the full catalogue after mount; SSR seed raised from 24 to 100.
Why: Whole categories looked empty.
Verified: Every category page checked for content

Item: Buy Now failed with "Could not start checkout"
What was wrong / what it is: Tebex Headless requires complete_url and cancel_url on basket creation; the seller and platform routes passed whatever the client sent, usually nothing.
Fix / What was built: Defaulted both to the app origin.
Why: Superseded later by the PayPal migration, but it unblocked sales at the time.
Verified: Buy Now completed

What was wrong / what it is: FiveM stores require the buyer to authenticate WITH THE STORE before a package can be added - not with the FiveCrux login.
Fix / What was built: Probe getBasketAuthUrl after creating the basket and redirect the buyer to Tebex auth when the store needs it.
Why: Surfaced to the user only as "Could not start checkout".
Verified: Tested against a store requiring auth

What was wrong / what it is: addPackageToBasket always sent quantity, but packages configured with disable_quantity: true reject it with "One of the options provided is invalid".
Fix / What was built: Only send quantity for genuine multi-quantity adds.
Why: This was the real cause of Buy Now failing after the store login step.
Verified: Buy Now completed on a disable_quantity package

Item: Buy Now moved to the seller's own store
What was wrong / what it is: Model B means each seller sells on their OWN webstore, which handles login, required package options and payment. The on-site basket could not satisfy such options.
Fix / What was built: Buy Now links to the package on the seller store; the import stores that URL, with a live resolve as fallback for older imports.
Why: Keeps FiveCrux out of merchant-of-record for seller sales.
Verified: Verified against a real seller store

What was wrong / what it is: The navbar linked to /scripts?category=other as a catch-all but no such row existed, so sellers could never pick it and the link showed an empty page since launch.
Fix / What was built: Removed the hardcoded entry; the real DB category now flows through the same list the navbar renders. A duplicate "Other" filter chip was removed with it.
Why: Confirmed: 0 assets had category='other'.
Verified: Link now resolves to real content

What was wrong / what it is: Category chips were a hardcoded list with singular slugs ("vehicle", "weapon") that never matched the DB's plural slugs.
Fix / What was built: Fetched from /api/categories like every other page. The asset-edit category dropdown had the same stale list and was fixed with it.
Why: Filters that silently return nothing read as an empty catalogue.
Verified: Every chip returns results

What was wrong / what it is: Each page hand-rolled its own chip row, so home showed "Peds" while scripts showed "Other", with different styling.
Fix / What was built: Extracted BrowseNav and used it on home, assets, props and giveaways. Category selection is URL-driven.
Why: Design direction: an identical chip row everywhere.
Verified: Compared side by side

Item: The props category filter was fake
What was wrong / what it is: The props page had category chips copied from scripts, but props have no category field anywhere in the data model - only the "Props" chip ever matched; the other four always returned zero.
Fix / What was built: Removed rather than reused.
Why: A filter that cannot work should not be shown.
Verified: Confirmed against the schema and the API

Item: "Trending This Week" was a duplicate row
What was wrong / what it is: trending and newReleases both did liveScripts.slice(0,12) - same items, same order. There is no per-week view tracking, so "This Week" was never a real claim.
Fix / What was built: Renamed to "Most Viewed" and sorted by actual view_count.
Why: The row was a copy of the one above it.
Verified: Rows now differ

What was wrong / what it is: The footer listed 4 fixed categories regardless of what the site actually had.
Fix / What was built: Reads the home-flagged categories from context, the same set and order as the nav.
Why: Stays in sync as categories change.
Verified: Verified after adding a category

What was wrong / what it is: The marketplace sells maps, vehicles, clothing and peds, not only scripts.
Fix / What was built: Every user-visible label renamed across 27 files. Routes, API paths, type names, query keys and category slugs deliberately unchanged so nothing breaks. MLOs were also relabelled to "Maps" with the slug preserved.
Why: Client request; display-only by design.
Verified: Build clean; all existing links still resolve

What was wrong / what it is: One giveaway can have several prizes handled by different people, but the delivery contact was stored once for the whole giveaway.
Fix / What was built: Stored and shown per prize. The top-level field was later removed entirely on request.
Why: Client request.
Verified: Create, edit and detail flows verified

What was wrong / what it is: Entry requirements could only belong to the whole giveaway.
Fix / What was built: giveaway_requirements gains a nullable prize_id (NULL = legacy giveaway-level task); each prize card has its own requirements editor and the detail page groups tasks under their prize.
Why: Client request; legacy giveaway-level tasks keep working.
Verified: Legacy and new giveaways both render correctly

What was wrong / what it is: One prize equals one place equals one winner, and the draw already picks one per prize - but the form let a creator type 5 and expect 5.
Fix / What was built: Removed the field; number_of_winners stays 1.
Why: The input promised something the draw would never do.
Verified: Draw behaviour unchanged

What was wrong / what it is: The 1-second countdown tick lived at page level and GiveawayCard was defined inside the component, so every tick re-rendered the page, remounted every card and reloaded all card images.
Fix / What was built: Moved the tick into its own module-scope Countdown component that owns its state.
Why: Visible flicker, worst on the ended tab.
Verified: Images no longer reload on tick

What was wrong / what it is: Pages wrap content in #0a0a0a but the footer's margin sits outside that wrapper, so the lighter body colour showed through as a band.
Fix / What was built: Set html and body to #0a0a0a.
Why: Root-caused instead of patching each page.
Verified: Gone site-wide

Item: Big empty gap beside the catalogue
What was wrong / what it is: Catalog grids used fixed 300px auto-fill columns with justify-center and a per-card width cap, so leftover space became large symmetric margins against the side rails. The cart had the same problem from a max-w-6xl cap.
Fix / What was built: Fluid responsive grid (1fr columns) with the card cap removed; cart main made full width while single-card states stay centered.
Why: Reported as dead space next to the rails.
Verified: Checked at several widths

What was wrong / what it is: Profile and admin sidebars stuck to the top but had no handling for their own overflow - it was simply cut off.
Fix / What was built: Capped to viewport height with independent scroll (scrollbar hidden), and the profile page restructured so only the main column scrolls.
Why: Needed lg:min-h-0 on the grid children - CSS Grid ignores height and overflow on items until min-height is reset from its auto default.
Verified: Tested with overflowing sidebar content

What was wrong / what it is: The profile dashboard was capped at max-w-[1320px] and centered, leaving large empty margins on wide screens, unlike the admin panel.
Fix / What was built: Removed the centering constraint.
Why: Consistency between the two dashboards.
Verified: Compared side by side

Item: The production build broke on an apostrophe
What was wrong / what it is: Next.js runs ESLint's react/no-unescaped-entities during the production build and fails on violations. A literal apostrophe broke the last two Vercel deploys - prod had been silently serving an older deployment.
Fix / What was built: Escaped it.
Why: A failed deploy is invisible unless you check: the site keeps serving the previous build.
Verified: npm run build completes

Item: The local seed corrupted its own data
What was wrong / what it is: scripts/setup-pglite.ts imported from lib/dev-auth.ts, which top-level-imports the live db client, silently opening a second PGlite connection on the same directory (PGlite allows one process per directory). The seed logged success but nothing persisted.
Fix / What was built: Split DEV_USERS into lib/dev-users.ts with no db import.
